items.stem: Define the term “a nucleosome”.
items.answer: The unit of chromatin formed by negatively charged DNA wrapped around a positively charged histone octamer.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the unit of chromatin formed by negatively charged DNA wrapped around a positively charged histone octamer.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about DNA structure, packaging and the search for genetic material is correct?
items.answer: The pitch of the DNA helix is 3.4 nm with about 10 bp per turn.
items.markingKey: (d) The pitch of the DNA helix is 3.4 nm with about 10 bp per turn. The other statements are false. They are rich in basic amino acids lysine and arginine and are positively charged. It is 0.34 nm; 3.4 nm is the pitch of one turn. Radioactive ³²P (DNA) entered the bacteria; ³⁵S (protein) stayed outside.
options: The distance between two consecutive base pairs in DNA is 3.4 nm.
Hershey and Chase found ³⁵S inside the infected bacteria.
Histones are rich in acidic amino acids.
The pitch of the DNA helix is 3.4 nm with about 10 bp per turn.

items.stem: A typical nucleosome contains about 200 bp of DNA helix. How many nucleosomes would be formed by a DNA segment of 2000 bp in a eukaryotic nucleus?
items.answer: 10 nucleosomes
items.markingKey: Number = total bp / bp per nucleosome = 2000/200 = 10 (1); each has a histone octamer around which DNA is wrapped (1).

items.stem: Which of the following shows the correct levels of DNA packaging in a eukaryotic nucleus?
items.answer: DNA double helix → nucleosome → chromatin fibre (beads-on-string) → chromosome
items.markingKey: (c) DNA double helix → nucleosome → chromatin fibre (beads-on-string) → chromosome. DNA wraps around histone octamers; nucleosomes coil into chromatin fibres that condense into chromosomes.
options: chromosome → DNA double helix → nucleosome → chromatin fibre (beads-on-string)
nucleosome → DNA double helix → chromatin fibre (beads-on-string) → chromosome
DNA double helix → nucleosome → chromatin fibre (beads-on-string) → chromosome
DNA double helix → chromosome → chromatin fibre (beads-on-string) → nucleosome

items.stem: Explain the term “DNA-dependent DNA polymerase”.
items.answer: The main enzyme that catalyses polymerisation of deoxynucleotides only in the 5′→3′ direction.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about DNA replication is correct?
items.answer: DNA polymerase can polymerise nucleotides only in the 5′→3′ direction.
items.markingKey: (a) DNA polymerase can polymerise nucleotides only in the 5′→3′ direction. The other statements are false. It polymerises only in the 5′→3′ direction. They are formed on the lagging strand (template 5′→3′). After two generations, equal amounts of hybrid and light DNA were found.
options: DNA polymerase can polymerise nucleotides only in the 5′→3′ direction.
After two generations in ¹⁴N medium, all DNA was hybrid.
Okazaki fragments are formed on the leading strand.
DNA polymerase polymerises in the 3′→5′ direction.

items.answer: A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Give two differences between the leading strand and the lagging strand.
items.answer: The leading strand: needs only one primer; template has 3′→5′ polarity. The lagging strand: synthesised discontinuously; fragments are joined by DNA ligase.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each correct, paired difference, e.g. the leading strand – needs only one primer; template has 3′→5′ polarity; the lagging strand – synthesised discontinuously; fragments are joined by DNA ligase.

items.answer: (i) The leading strand (ii) template has 3′→5′ polarity (iii) forms Okazaki fragments; fragments are joined by DNA ligase

items.answer: (a) The lagging strand: synthesised discontinuously; template has 5′→3′ polarity; forms Okazaki fragments. The leading strand: synthesised continuously; template has 3′→5′ polarity; needs only one primer. (b) The lagging strand.

items.stem: Why is replication discontinuous on one strand? Name the enzyme that joins the fragments.
items.answer: The two strands are antiparallel and DNA polymerase can add nucleotides only in the 5′→3′ direction; so on the template with 5′→3′ polarity the new strand is made in short Okazaki fragments, which are joined by DNA ligase.
items.markingKey: 1 mark reason; 1 mark ligase.

items.stem: Define the term “aminoacylation”.
items.answer: The charging of tRNA, in which an amino acid is activated in the presence of ATP and linked to its tRNA.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about transcription, genetic code and translation is correct?

items.answer: (i) Without lactose, the repressor bound the operator and blocked transcription. (ii) Lactose (allolactose). (iii) Lactose binds the repressor and inactivates it; the repressor leaves the operator and RNA polymerase transcribes z, y and a genes.

items.stem: Give two differences between gene content and repetitive sequences.
items.answer: Gene content: dystrophin is the largest known gene (2.4 million bases); function unknown for over 50% of discovered genes. Repetitive sequences: used in DNA fingerprinting; repeated hundreds to thousands of times.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each correct, paired difference, e.g. gene content – dystrophin is the largest known gene (2.4 million bases); function unknown for over 50% of discovered genes; repetitive sequences – used in DNA fingerprinting; repeated hundreds to thousands of times.

items.stem: Which term describes densely packed, darkly stained chromatin that is transcriptionally inactive?
items.answer: heterochromatin
items.markingKey: (c) Heterochromatin: densely packed, darkly stained chromatin that is transcriptionally inactive.
options: transformation
Chargaff's rule
heterochromatin
a nucleoside

items.stem: Which of the following statements about DNA replication is correct?
items.answer: DNA polymerase can polymerise nucleotides only in the 5′→3′ direction.
items.markingKey: (d) DNA polymerase can polymerise nucleotides only in the 5′→3′ direction. The other statements are false. It polymerises only in the 5′→3′ direction. They are formed on the lagging strand (template 5′→3′). It occurs in the S phase; failure of cell division after replication gives polyploidy.
options: Replication in eukaryotes occurs in the M phase.
Okazaki fragments are formed on the leading strand.
DNA polymerase polymerises in the 3′→5′ direction.
DNA polymerase can polymerise nucleotides only in the 5′→3′ direction.

items.stem: An mRNA has the sequence 5′-AUGCAAUUCGUCAAAUGGUAA-3′. Using the genetic code, write the polypeptide formed and state how many amino acids it has. (AAA = Lys, CAA = Gln, GUC = Val, UGG = Trp, UUC = Phe; AUG = Met; UAA = stop)
items.answer: Met–Gln–Phe–Val–Lys–Trp (6 amino acids)
items.markingKey: Translation starts at AUG (Met) and reads triplets without gaps (1); UAA is a stop codon with no tRNA, so translation ends: Met–Gln–Phe–Val–Lys–Trp = 6 amino acids (1).

items.stem:
Assertion (A): DNA fingerprinting is used in paternity disputes.
Reason (R): Each person inherits half of their VNTR alleles from each parent.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) Bands can be matched to parents.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: A classic experiment showed this: identified DNA as the transforming principle; purified biochemicals from heat-killed S cells; DNase stopped transformation. Which experiment is described? Give a reason.
items.answer: Avery, MacLeod and McCarty's work
items.markingKey: 1 mark: Avery, MacLeod and McCarty's work; 1 mark: the features identified DNA as the transforming principle; purified biochemicals from heat-killed S cells; DNase stopped transformation are characteristic of it.

items.stem: Which term describes the DNA sequence next to the promoter to which the repressor binds?
items.answer: the operator
items.markingKey: (c) The operator: the DNA sequence next to the promoter to which the repressor binds.
options: negative regulation
an operon
the operator
an inducer

items.stem: In eukaryotes, what does RNA polymerase II transcribe?
items.answer: the precursor of mRNA (hnRNA)
items.markingKey: (a) RNA polymerase II transcribes the precursor of mRNA (hnRNA).
options: the precursor of mRNA (hnRNA)
DNA from an RNA template
the Okazaki fragments of DNA
rRNAs (28S, 18S and 5.8S)

items.stem:
A structure or molecule involved in gene expression has these features: promoter is towards the 5′ end of the coding strand; coding strand has the same sequence as RNA except T for U; only the template strand is transcribed.
(i) Identify it. (1 mark)
(ii) State one more feature you would expect to observe. (1 mark)
(iii) How would the observations differ if it were the ribosome? Give two points. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) The transcription unit (ii) has a promoter, structural gene and terminator (iii) site of peptide bond formation; larger subunit has two sites for tRNA
items.markingKey: (i) the transcription unit – 1 mark. (ii) any one of: has a promoter, structural gene and terminator – 1 mark. (iii) for the ribosome: made of rRNA and proteins; two subunits; site of peptide bond formation – 1 mark each for any two.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “Histones are rich in acidic amino acids.”
items.answer: They are rich in basic amino acids lysine and arginine and are positively charged.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: They are rich in basic amino acids lysine and arginine and are positively charged.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Histones are rich in acidic amino acids.
Reason (R): Histones are rich in the basic amino acids lysine and arginine.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A is false: They are rich in basic amino acids lysine and arginine and are positively charged. R is a true statement.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “Replication in eukaryotes occurs in the M phase.”
items.answer: It occurs in the S phase; failure of cell division after replication gives polyploidy.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: It occurs in the S phase; failure of cell division after replication gives polyploidy.

items.stem:
During replication a strand shows these features: template has 3′→5′ polarity; synthesised towards the replication fork; needs only one primer.
(i) Which strand is it? (1 mark)
(ii) State one more feature you would expect to observe. (1 mark)
(iii) How would the observations differ if it were the lagging strand? Give two points. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) The leading strand (ii) synthesised continuously (iii) fragments are joined by DNA ligase; forms Okazaki fragments
items.markingKey: (i) the leading strand – 1 mark. (ii) any one of: synthesised continuously – 1 mark. (iii) for the lagging strand: synthesised discontinuously; template has 5′→3′ polarity; forms Okazaki fragments – 1 mark each for any two.

items.stem: In the lac operon, which product is coded by the lac y?
items.answer: permease
items.markingKey: (c) Lac y codes for permease, which increases permeability of the cell to β-galactosides.
options: transacetylase
repressor
permease
β-galactosidase

items.stem: Which term describes expressed sequence tags, used to identify the genes expressed as RNA?
items.answer: ESTs
items.markingKey: (c) ESTs: expressed sequence tags, used to identify the genes expressed as RNA.
options: the Human Genome Project
DNA fingerprinting
ESTs
VNTR

items.stem: Which of the following statements about Human Genome Project and DNA fingerprinting is incorrect?
items.answer: The Y chromosome has the largest number of genes.
items.markingKey: (a) The incorrect statement is “The Y chromosome has the largest number of genes.” Correct form: Chromosome 1 has the most genes; Y has the fewest.
options: The Y chromosome has the largest number of genes.
The human genome has about 3 × 10⁹ bp.
About 1.4 million single base DNA differences (SNPs) were identified.
Less than 2% of the genome codes for proteins.

items.stem: Arrange the following in the correct sequence of events in DNA replication: unwinding at ori, formation of replication fork, joining of Okazaki fragments by ligase, polymerisation 5′→3′. Give a reason.
items.answer: unwinding at ori → formation of replication fork → polymerisation 5′→3′ → joining of Okazaki fragments by ligase
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the order unwinding at ori → formation of replication fork → polymerisation 5′→3′ → joining of Okazaki fragments by ligase; 1 mark for the reason: The helix opens at the origin, synthesis proceeds at the fork and ligase seals fragments.

items.stem: What is the function of rRNA?
items.answer: plays structural and catalytic role during translation
items.markingKey: (b) RRNA: plays structural and catalytic role during translation.
options: brings amino acids and reads the genetic code (adapter molecule)
plays structural and catalytic role during translation
provides the template for translation
the primary transcript in eukaryotes that is processed into mRNA

items.stem: Give two differences between lac y and the i gene.
items.answer: Lac y: helps lactose enter the cell; codes for permease. The i gene: regulatory gene; codes for the repressor.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each correct, paired difference, e.g. lac y – helps lactose enter the cell; codes for permease; the i gene – regulatory gene; codes for the repressor.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about transcription, genetic code and translation is correct?
items.answer: The ribosome itself acts as a catalyst (ribozyme) for peptide bond formation.
items.markingKey: (c) The ribosome itself acts as a catalyst (ribozyme) for peptide bond formation. The other statements are false. It is unambiguous and specific: one codon codes for only one amino acid. There are no tRNAs for stop codons. RNA polymerase II transcribes the precursor of mRNA (hnRNA); RNA polymerase III makes tRNA, 5S rRNA and snRNAs.
options: The genetic code is ambiguous.
Stop codons have specific tRNAs.
The ribosome itself acts as a catalyst (ribozyme) for peptide bond formation.
RNA polymerase III transcribes mRNA in eukaryotes.

items.stem: Give two differences between repetitive sequences and gene content.
items.answer: Repetitive sequences: form a large part of the genome; repeated hundreds to thousands of times. Gene content: about 20,500 genes; average gene 3000 bases.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each correct, paired difference, e.g. repetitive sequences – form a large part of the genome; repeated hundreds to thousands of times; gene content – about 20,500 genes; average gene 3000 bases.

items.stem: Which term describes a nucleoside with a phosphate group linked to the 5′-OH through a phosphoester linkage?
items.answer: a nucleotide
items.markingKey: (b) A nucleotide: a nucleoside with a phosphate group linked to the 5′-OH through a phosphoester linkage.
options: heterochromatin
a nucleotide
a nucleoside
Chargaff's rule

items.stem: Which of the following statements about DNA replication is correct?
items.answer: Replication occurs in the S phase of the cell cycle.
items.markingKey: (b) Replication occurs in the S phase of the cell cycle. The other statements are false. It polymerises only in the 5′→3′ direction. They are formed on the lagging strand (template 5′→3′). After two generations, equal amounts of hybrid and light DNA were found.
options: Okazaki fragments are formed on the leading strand.
Replication occurs in the S phase of the cell cycle.
After two generations in ¹⁴N medium, all DNA was hybrid.
DNA polymerase polymerises in the 3′→5′ direction.

items.stem: An mRNA has the sequence 5′-AUGGAUGGCCUUUAG-3′. Using the genetic code, write the polypeptide formed and state how many amino acids it has. (CUU = Leu, GAU = Asp, GGC = Gly; AUG = Met; UAG = stop)
items.answer: Met–Asp–Gly–Leu (4 amino acids)
items.markingKey: Translation starts at AUG (Met) and reads triplets without gaps (1); UAG is a stop codon with no tRNA, so translation ends: Met–Asp–Gly–Leu = 4 amino acids (1).
